questions.question: On whose advice does the Governor appoint the ministers?
questions.solution: According to Article 164, the Governor first appoints the Chief Minister. Subsequently, the other ministers are appointed by the Governor specifically on the advice of the Chief Minister.

questions.question: Who unfurls the flag at Rajpath on the Republic Day?
questions.solution: The President of India, as the Head of State, unfurls the national flag at Rajpath (now Kartavya Path) during the Republic Day celebrations. The Prime Minister hoists the flag on Independence Day at the Red Fort.

questions.question: The Governor’s emoluments are decided by the:
questions.solution: While the President appoints the Governor, the Parliament has the power to determine the Governor's emoluments, allowances, and privileges by law.

questions.question: The ministers in the state hold office during the pleasure of the:
questions.solution: Under Article 164(1), although ministers are chosen based on the CM's advice, they legally hold their office during the pleasure of the Governor.

questions.question: In which year did Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan assume office as the first Vice-President of India?
questions.solution: Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan became the first Vice-President of India in 1952 and served two terms until 1962. His birthday, September 5th, is celebrated as Teachers' Day.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that ‘The President shall, notwithstanding the expiration of his/her term, continue to hold office until his successor enters upon his/her office’?
questions.solution: Article 56 defines the term of the President (5 years). To prevent a vacuum in the highest office, it specifies that the outgoing President continues to hold office until the new successor is ready to take charge.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that an election to fill a vacancy caused by the expiration of the term of office of the President shall be completed before the expiration of the term?
questions.solution: Article 62 mandates that the election to replace a President whose term is ending must be finished before that term expires. If a vacancy occurs due to death or resignation, the election must happen within six months.

questions.question: Who was the second vice-President of India?
questions.solution: Dr. Zakir Hussain served as the second Vice-President (1962–1967). He later became the third President of India and was the first to die in office.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 112 provides for the annual financial statement at the Union level.
2. Article 202 provides for the annual financial statement at the State level, which is laid before the Legislature by the Governor.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution: Both statements are correct. Article 112 describes the Union Budget (Annual Financial Statement), and Article 202 describes the State Budget.

questions.question: When the President of India keeps a bill (except money bill and constitutional amendment bill) pending for an indefinite period, it is called______.
questions.solution: In a Pocket Veto, the President neither ratifies nor rejects nor returns the bill, but simply keeps it pending indefinitely. Since the Constitution does not give a time limit for the President to act on a bill, this effectively kills the bill.

questions.question: The Governor of an Indian state before entering upon his office takes an oath or affirmation before ____________.
questions.option_1: the Chief Justice of the High Court exercising jurisdiction in relation to the State
questions.option_3: the Chief Minister of the concerned state
questions.solution: Under Article 159, the oath of office to the Governor is administered by the Chief Justice of the High Court of that state. In their absence, the senior-most judge of that court performs the duty.

questions.question: What is the duty of the Chief Minister, as mentioned under Article 167 of the Indian Constitution?
questions.option_1: Communication of all decisions of the Council of Ministers to the Governor.
questions.option_2: Appointment and removal of Council of the Ministers.
questions.option_3: Appointment of the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly.
questions.option_4: Appointment of Advocate General of the state in consultation with Attorney general.
questions.solution: Article 167 defines the CM as the link between the Cabinet and the Governor. It is the CM's duty to communicate all decisions of the Council of Ministers to the Governor regarding administration and legislative proposals.

questions.question: Who among the following served the shortest tenure as the Prime Minister of India?
questions.solution: Among the specific list provided in the options, Chandra Shekhar (Nov 1990 – June 1991) had the shortest tenure. Note: Gulzarilal Nanda holds the record for the shortest tenure overall as an acting PM.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Inter-State Council:
1. It is established under Article 263 of the Constitution.
2. It is chaired by the Prime Minister of India.
3. It consists of four Cabinet Ministers of the Union Council of Ministers nominated by the Prime Minister.
4. Chief Ministers of all States are its members.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution: Statements 1, 2, and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because the council actually includes six Union Cabinet Ministers nominated by the Prime Minister, not four.

questions.question: Who appoints the Chief Justice of India?
questions.solution: Under Article 124(2), the President has the power to appoint the Chief Justice of India and other judges of the Supreme Court.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the qualifications for the appointment of a Governor in India:
A. A person must be a citizen of India and must have completed 35 years of age.
B. The minimum age required to contest for the Lok Sabha election is 30 years.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution: Statement A is correct (Article 157). Statement B is incorrect because the minimum age for Lok Sabha is 25 years (30 years is required for Rajya Sabha).

questions.question: Who administers the Union Territories of India?
questions.solution: Under Article 239, Union Territories are administered by the President, acting through an administrator (Lieutenant Governor or Administrator) appointed by him.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding the benefits of the retired President of India?
A. The former President of India will also be entitled to a monthly pension of ₹2.5 lakh.
B. He/She is entitled to a secretarial staff comprising a private secretary, a personal assistant, an additional private secretary, two peons, and office expenses up to ₹1 lakh per annum.
C. He/She is also entitled to free highest-class travel anywhere in India, accompanied by one person, by rail, air, or steamer.
questions.solution: All three statements (A, B, and C) correctly describe the post-retirement benefits and perks provided to a former President of India to maintain their dignity and facilitate their ongoing public life.

questions.question: Who among the following Presidents of India was also the deputy chairman of the Planning Commission?
questions.solution: Dr. Pranab Mukherjee had an extensive administrative career before becoming the 13th President. He served as the Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission from 1991 to 1996.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Vice President of India is INCORRECT?
questions.option_1: Members of State legislatures do not take part in his elections.
questions.option_2: He acts as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
questions.option_3: The Vice President is elected for five years.
questions.option_4: He can be removed from his office by the President approved through a resolution passed by the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.
questions.solution: Statement (d) is incorrect. The Vice President is removed by a resolution of the Rajya Sabha passed by an effective majority and agreed to by the Lok Sabha. The President does not remove him through a simple approval of a resolution.

questions.question: The emoluments and allowances of the President and other expenditure relating to his office is charged on the ______ of India.
questions.solution: The salaries and allowances of constitutional authorities like the President are charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India (Article 266). This means they are not subject to the annual vote of Parliament, ensuring independence.

questions.question: Which is NOT correct about the powers of the Chief Minister?
questions.option_2: He presides over the meetings of the Council of Ministers.
questions.option_3: When he resigns or dies, it has no effect in the functioning of the council of ministers.
questions.option_4: The Governor appoints ministers on His recommendations.
questions.solution:
The Chief Minister is the head of the Council of Ministers. Because the council's existence depends on the Chief Minister, his resignation or death automatically dissolves the council. Other powers include:
  • Allocating and reshuffling portfolios.
  • Presiding over cabinet meetings.
  • Acting as the primary link between the Governor and the cabinet (Article 167).

questions.question: Who among the following is NOT appointed by the President of India?
questions.option_2: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
questions.solution:
The Solicitor General of India is appointed by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC), not directly by the President. In contrast:
  • Attorney General: Appointed by the President under Article 76.
  • CAG: Appointed by the President under Article 148.
  • Ambassadors: Appointed by the President to represent India abroad.

questions.question: Who among the following was the third Vice-President of India?
questions.solution:
The sequence of the first few Vice-Presidents is:
  1. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan
  2. Zakir Hussain
  3. V. V. Giri
  4. Gopal Swarup Pathak
  5. B. D. Jatti

questions.question: The election of the next Vice-President is to be held within _____ of the expiry of the term of office of the outgoing Vice-President.
questions.solution: Under the Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections Act, and in accordance with the spirit of Article 66, the election to fill a vacancy caused by the expiration of the term of office of the Vice-President must be completed within 60 days before the term expires.
